hypothesis: Adding a Laplacian-style penalty sum over net pins of crit_i*crit_j*(p_i-p_j)^2 (critical-pair locality, star-expanded per net) will keep adjacent timing-critical nodes on the same tier, directly attacking the crit-pair cross-tier fraction that the baseline leaves nonzero on C3.
analysis:
(1) No. The critical-pair penalty did not reduce crit_cross on C3 (0.069→0.073) and C3 regressed (score −0.032, dWNS −5.5%); C1 crit_cross also rose (0.011→0.016) despite its score gain.

(2) C1 improved via wcut (421→406) but with more repair_flips (103→121) and higher crit_cross—gain likely from cut/weighted-cut, not the penalty. C2 flat (crit_cross already 0). C3 barely changed (3.2% flips) yet worsened, suggesting the penalty perturbed tiers without fixing critical pairs.

(3) No: seed_std 0.053, robust mean −0.023, min −0.032—spread swamps the mean.

(4) Ablate the penalty weight and log crit-pair cross-tier directly per seed on C3 before retuning.
